roadmap_item: RI-UIX08 / the dialogue window's input path
could_not_do: FAULT 2 IS NOT FIXED. The character-creation flow still draws on render/ui.js's old vellum reply panel. I ruled against forcing it and the ruling with its evidence is under `fault_2_ruling`. It is reversible and names what would overturn it.

M2 — CLICKING AN INLINE LINK — IS UNMEASURED, and this is the largest hole in this piece. At helstrom-market the conversation produces 0 inline links after all 12 column topics are asked, so there was no topic_link element on screen to click. That is the content gap engine.js:3600 already records (81 of 1,216 topic unlocks are named in the text that unlocks them, 6.7%), not an input defect. reports/uix08/probe-stormhold/window-probe.json shows stormhold-street DOES produce links; I started that run three times and killed it after ~40 minutes of wall clock without a single line of output, with the box at load 22-29 over 4 cores and five other agents' browsers resident. WHAT I CAN SAY: the link branch and the column branch share pickHit(), dialoguePointer(), the arm/confirm pair and _dialogueConfirm(); they differ in one line (`hit.pane === 'prose'` sets linkIdx instead of rowIdx). That is an argument from shared code, NOT a measurement, and it must not be quoted as one.

K5 — FOLLOWING AN INLINE LINK BY KEYBOARD — is unmeasured for the identical reason (0 links at helstrom-market). Note this is also the check the previous builder's report flagged as failing ('D2 following a link APPENDS'); I did not get to reproduce it as a real failure.

GAMEPAD ARM NOT DRIVEN. No pad shim is wired into this probe, so the gamepad leg of CRITIC-DOCTRINE 1.2b clause 4 is scored 0 fail-closed, not passed. What I did for the pad is code, not measurement: _conversationSync now sets real.pad.uiMode = true while a conversation is open, because input/gamepad.js:535 maps the D-pad hat onto uiMove only under that flag — so before this, on the GameSir X2s the owner plays on, the D-pad did nothing in this window and only the left stick walked the column. UNMEASURED.

THE CENSUS WALK ARM (C1) DID NOT COMPLETE. `--census` drives censusBegin({}) and reads which surface draws each creation node; it hung under load and I killed it. The fault-2 conclusion below does NOT depend on it — it is read directly from the source, and the source is dispositive.

PERSUASION IS STILL A CONTROL THAT LOOKS DEAD. Confirming the Persuasion action row through the real key path moved the disposition bar 69 -> 69 and added no prose. conversationPersuade() does write sim.quest.dispositions[eid] = before + r.permChange, so this is either permChange 0 on that roll or a derived-disposition read that does not see the register. NOT DIAGNOSED. Measured and reported rather than guessed at.

`node tools/contention.mjs --gate` said WAIT and I proceeded anyway, one browser at a time, sequentially. Rule 21 says say so; this is me saying so. Every browser figure in this file was taken with 4-5 other agents' browsers resident and load 22-29 over 4 cores.

No screenshots. The evidence here is the state after each interaction, which is what 1.2b clause 5 asks for. A still of this window is precisely the evidence that already passed while it was unusable.
headline: The keyboard was never broken. There was NO POINTER PATH AT ALL — ui/system.js's own rule 2 says 'no cursor, no hover, no drag, no click target' — so on the desktop build every drawn control in the dialogue window was inert to a mouse. The owner plays in a browser.

measured_before_the_fix.instrument: tools/ui/dialogue-drive-probe.mjs — real DOM KeyboardEvent / MouseEvent / PointerEvent only. Nothing in it calls a function the UI calls and nothing sets UI state, which is the whole difference from tools/ui/dialogue-window-probe.mjs (that one assigns `eng._convPending` and writes `eng.ui.dialogueFocus` directly, which is why it scored 22/25 on a window that could not be used).
measured_before_the_fix.keyboard_PASSED: ArrowRight prose->column; ArrowDown row 0->1; KeyE answered and the transcript went 1 -> 6 lines with heading 'dying far from the tree'; Goodbye closed it; Space backed out.
measured_before_the_fix.mouse_FAILED: click a column topic: 2 -> 2 lines, nothing. click Goodbye: window open true -> true, nothing.
measured_before_the_fix.touch_FAILED: tap a column topic: 2 -> 2 lines, nothing (and see the instrument note below — the first touch FAIL was my own probe's fault).
measured_before_the_fix.dead_controls: 10 of 12 column rows answered. Persuasion did nothing visible; re-asking the topic that was already the last block printed nothing.

instrument_traps_i_walked_into_and_had_t: RUN 1 REPORTED EVERY KEYBOARD CHECK AS FAIL, AGAINST A GAME THAT WAS FINE. `?harness=1` makes Engine.setMode('harness') call real.detach(), so a KeyboardEvent dispatched at the page reaches nothing. Fixed by setMode('play-instrumented') (A-JRN1: real listeners, harness clock) and by adding check I0, which presses a key and asserts the pipeline's own moveX/pendingPress moved BEFORE any other check is believed. A probe that cannot succeed is as bad as one that cannot fail.

TOUCH HAD THE SAME SHAPE. input/real.js applyDeviceClass() attaches the touch listeners only on device class 'handheld'; on a desktop class they are detached. Fixed with setViewport({pointer:'coarse'}) plus check I1, which asserts touch.enabled && touch.attached && the surface hook is a function.

the_fix.one_sentence: The dialogue window now publishes the rects it drew, and a click or tap on one of them moves the SAME caret a stick moves and confirms through the SAME function a button press confirms through.
the_fix.game/src/ui/screens/dialogue.js: drawDialogue builds a `hits` list in the same pass that declares the elements, from the same rects, so what you can click and what you can see cannot drift. Publishes `hits`, `hit_count`, `panel_rect`. Link rects are padded toward RI-UIX06 B4's 44 CSS px touch floor, capped at half the line pitch so consecutive lines cannot overlap. DialogueHistory.append takes a sequence number.
the_fix.game/src/ui/system.js: dialoguePointer(x,y,phase): hit-test topmost-first (paint order), move the one focus model, arm on press, confirm only when the release lands on the same control, swallow clicks inside the panel that hit nothing (otherwise Mouse0 = light swings your weapon at the person you are talking to). dialogueStep consumes the confirm and routes it through the new _dialogueConfirm(), which is now the single place any device's confirm is turned into an action.
the_fix.game/src/input/real.js: onSurfacePointer hook on mousedown / mouseup / mousemove. On mousedown it sits after _captureControl and BEFORE _down and before the pointer-lock request. The mousemove leg is what finally makes RI-UIX08 §C's `link_over` reachable — the window shipped a three-state colour ramp with nothing in the build able to be 'over' anything.
the_fix.game/src/input/touch.js: onSurfacePointer hook in down() before _hitButton AND before the stick claims the left half of the screen (T2), which is where the prose pane sits; and in up(), replaying the down position because up(id,event) carries no coordinates.
the_fix.game/src/engine.js: _bindSurfacePointer() owns the client-px -> menus-canvas-px conversion in ONE place, recomputed per event from getBoundingClientRect and the drawing-buffer size (they differ by dpr, and by a different factor per axis on a letterboxed canvas). _conversationSync releases pointer lock while a conversation is open — with the lock held there is no cursor and clientX/clientY are meaningless — and sets pad.uiMode. _dlgSaySeq bumps on every completed say, which is what lets a re-ask reprint.

verified_after_the_fix.T1_tap_a_column_topic: PASS, on a forced coarse-pointer device class with I1 proving the touch listeners were attached first. 1 -> 6 lines.
verified_after_the_fix.X1_DELETE_THE_FIX: PASS, and this is the control the whole claim rests on. With `real.onSurfacePointer` nulled — the ONE seam this fix adds — the identical click on the identical row gives 7 -> 7 lines and 2 -> 2 blocks. That is exactly the behaviour the owner reported. The hook was confirmed present before removal, so the teardown is not inert.
verified_after_the_fix.K4_improved: 10 of 12 -> 11 of 12 column rows answer. The row that came back to life is the re-ask, which the said_seq change fixed. Persuasion is still the one dead row.
verified_after_the_fix.keyboard_unchanged: K1, K2, K3, K3b, K5a, K6a, K6, K7 all still PASS. A route was added; none was removed.

fault_2_ruling.what_the_flow_actually_uses_read_from_th: engine.js `_censusSync()` calls `buildCensusModel(...)` (character/scene.js:372) and `renderer.ui.setModel(model)` — render/ui.js's bottom-anchored vellum panel. `_conversationSync()` sets the same model and then calls `renderer.ui.setSuppressed(DIALOGUE_WINDOW)`, which is the ONE line that hands a conversation to the new window. It is never called on the census path. That is the whole of why they diverged.
fault_2_ruling.node_census_grep: grep -o '"kind": *"[a-z]*"' game/data/dialogue/topics/writ-house.json | sort | uniq -c => 8 choice, 4 pick, 3 text, 1 questionnaire, 1 observed, 2 conditional.
fault_2_ruling.the_ruling: I did NOT route it, and I did not route it PARTLY. A partial route is the worse option and _conversationSync's own comment is the argument: 'TWO WINDOWS FOR ONE CONVERSATION WOULD BE WORSE THAN EITHER'. A new player would meet the RI-UIX08 window on the 8 choice nodes and the old vellum panel on the name, the class picks and the birthsign, inside one five-minute scene.
fault_2_ruling.the_blocker_named_precisely: A full route needs three affordances the window has no element for, and RI-UIX08 §A is titled 'What is on screen. Six elements, no more' — so adding a seventh is a hard fail of the item being satisfied. The three: (1) multi-select state for the 4 `pick` nodes (render/ui.js:476-478 draws it as a '· ' prefix and a colour); (2) the typed name for the 3 `text` nodes (render/ui.js:457-458 draws `typed + '▁'`) — dropping it regresses RI-JRN01 O17's 'typing on a keyboard still works and overrides whatever is highlighted'; (3) the aside 'She is waiting for 2 more' (scene.js:425). Two more elements are meaningless during creation and would have to be HIDDEN, which is allowed because hiding is not adding: the disposition bar (§A5) and Goodbye (§A6, 'the only way out that the window advertises' — during creation there is none).
fault_2_ruling.what_is_NOT_a_blocker_checked_rather_tha: RI-JRN01 O8/M5 does NOT conflict. M5 requires creation inputs to happen with the world visible, opaque UI <= 55% of frame area, hard fail on a uniform background over >= 90%. The RI-UIX08 window is a floating translucent panel (interior alpha 0.84) at ~57% width x ~76% height ~= 43% of frame over the running world. I checked this because the code comment in character/scene.js asserts a 42%-of-frame-height strip rule and I did not want to inherit it unread.
fault_2_ruling.what_would_overturn_this: A ruling that RI-UIX08 §A's 'no seventh element' does not bind a creation variant of the window, or an amendment adding the three affordances as a §A-sanctioned creation mode. Either makes the route buildable in roughly the shape sketched under `fault_2_spec`.

fault_2_spec.seam: _censusSync(): build a dialogue-window model from the census state and call renderer.ui.setSuppressed(true), exactly as _conversationSync does. UISystem needs a `censusModel` branch beside `_dialogueModel`.
fault_2_spec.mapping: speaker = model.speaker_name (+ title); blocks = spoken[] then preamble then line, as prose; column = surface.options (label = option.text); actions = []; disposition = null -> hide element 5; goodbye = null -> hide element 6.
fault_2_spec.picked_without_a_new_element: when a pick lands, append it to the PROSE ('You name Long Blade.') so the picked state lives in the transcript, which is the window's own mechanism. The 'waiting for N more' aside is already authored in her voice and can be a prose block.
fault_2_spec.the_one_that_needs_a_bar_decision: the typed name. There is no text affordance in the six elements and O17 requires keyboard typing to keep working.
fault_2_spec.must_re_run_after: every RI-JRN01 row that measures the creation scene, M5 above all, since the surface geometry changes.
